about.title: Personal Injury Help in Beverly Hills, California
about.longDescription: Beverly Hills sees real traffic on corridors like Wilshire Boulevard, Olympic Boulevard, N Santa Monica Boulevard, and Sunset Boulevard, and public records reflect that: 378 injury collisions and 524 people injured in the most recent final reporting year, with reported crashes tending to peak on Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. If you were one of those people, or you love someone who was, you're likely dealing with medical appointments, missed work, and a lot of unanswered questions right now. That's where we come in. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with an independent personal injury attorney who can review what happened and explain your options. We are not a law firm, and we don't handle your case ourselves. We simply make the introduction so you can talk to someone who understands California injury law and can tell you where you stand. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover money. There's no pressure and no cost to find out if you have a case worth pursuing after a Beverly Hills crash.

whyChoose.title: What You Should Know Before You Wait

items.title: Your Filing Window Is Limited
items.desc: California law generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim. If a government entity was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so timing matters.

items.title: Partial Fault Won't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you were partly responsible for the crash, you can still recover compensation reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Cap on What You Can Recover for Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain, suffering, and emotional distress.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Unless You Win
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost and no fee unless your case results in a recovery.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Beverly Hills?
items.answer: Under California law, you generally have two years from the date of the injury to file a lawsuit. If your claim involves a city or county entity, that deadline can be much shorter, sometimes just six months, so it's worth checking early.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the crash?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame. Your total recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault, not eliminated.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Beverly Hills?
items.answer: Public records show higher collision counts along corridors such as Wilshire Boulevard, Olympic Boulevard, N Santa Monica Boulevard, and Sunset Boulevard, with reported crashes often peaking on Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. These are simply reported counts, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: No. In standard personal injury cases, California does not cap non-economic damages like pain and suffering. Compensation depends on the specifics of your injury and case.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and we are not a law firm ourselves. Attorneys in the network work on contingency, so you don't pay unless they win your case.
